newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yen-denominated repo pacts up to Bnk of Japan--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Yen-denominated repo pacts up to Bnk of Japan--MOF.

text.p: A senior official of Japan's Ministry of Finance said on Wednesday the Bank of Japan will have to weigh the merits of yen-denominated repurchase agreements amongst regional central banks.

"Well, it's up to the Bank of Japan to consider," Takatoshi Kato, Vice-Minister of Finance for International Affairs, told Reuters Financial Television at the World Economic Forum meeting in Hong Kong.

"I think it depends upon whether the repo arrangements are of a nature of very acute, emergency type liquidity problem scheme, or... it is more perceived as within the business of a central bank, or whether that scheme assumes the character of essentially the provision of a loan -- a credit to the counterpart," Kato said in the interview.

Over the past year, Asian central banks, led largely by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, have organised a series of bilateral U.S. dollar repo agreements meant to act as a safety net to provide liquidity in times of currency crisis.
The subject has been a topic at the Hong Kong meeting, which focused on European and East Asian economic interplay.
Delegates discussed the possibility of a yen-denominated safety net to complement the existing web of U.S. dollar bilateral agreements.
